samples.question: The picture shows four vessels standing side by side. A vessel is drawn as a vertical stack of square unit cells: the number of cells in a stack is that vessel's capacity, that is, the largest number of units it can hold, and it never holds more. The dark blue cells, which always sit at the bottom of a stack, are the units the vessel holds to begin with, and the light grey cells above them are its free space. Different vessels may have different capacities and different starting amounts. Under each vessel there is one coloured disc, and the four disc colours, green, orange, purple and yellow, are all different, so a vessel is named by the colour of its own disc. Below the vessels there is a row of five cream cards, and each card is one pour. A card carries two small discs coloured like two of the vessel discs and one black arrow drawn between them: the card pours from the vessel named by the disc at the arrow's tail, the plain end, into the vessel named by the disc the arrowhead points at. A pour moves as many whole units as it can, which is the smaller of two amounts: the number of units the source vessel is holding at that moment, and the free space still left in the target vessel at that moment. So the pour stops as soon as the source is empty or the target is full, whichever happens first, and any units it could not move stay in the source vessel. Nothing is spilled or created: the units a pour moves leave the source and arrive in the target. The cards act one at a time, in order from the leftmost card to the rightmost card, as the grey arrow below the row shows, and the amounts the vessels hold keep changing as later cards act. A red ring marks one of the vessel discs: the marked vessel is the one whose disc centre is nearest to the centre of that red ring. The amounts the vessels hold after the cards have acted are not drawn anywhere; only the starting stacks are drawn. After all five cards have acted in order from left to right, how many units does the marked vessel hold? Answer with a single number.
